_note:
Batch 36 — five translation tools, book-scoped.

🔴 WHY THE SEEDS ARE SQL. Four of these five need a translation VERSION to exist (base_version_id, edited_from_version_id, version_id) or a JOB (job_id), and the only tool path to either is translation_start_job — which SPENDS. The standing rule is that a card for a cost-bearing tool is never approved, so the tool path is closed to this loop by design. Batch 25 set the precedent for exactly this shape: when the only way to reach a state is a confirm-gated tool the loop must not drive, seed the state in SQL and SELECT-verify it. Every seeded row is scoped to the throwaway book and dies with it.

The schema was READ, not guessed: chapter_translations.job_id is NOT NULL and FKs to translation_jobs(job_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so the job row comes first and the version hangs off it. Both tables' NOT NULL columns and defaults were listed before these inserts were written — the batch-32 lesson, where one guessed column name cost all 25 runs. The new preflight also executes every seed assertion before the batch spends a turn.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASKED: translation_job_control's enum offers cancel | pause | resume | retry, and its own description says 'resume' and 'retry' RE-SPEND money and return a cost estimate + confirm token. The scenario asks to CANCEL — free and immediate — because asking for a resume would be asking the model to reach for a cost-bearing action the loop then refuses to approve, which measures the harness's rule rather than the tool.

scenarios.prompt: Set the target language for this book's translation to Vietnamese.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['set target language'] + ['translation settings'], verbatim, plus the language so the CONTENT is the author's.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM book_translation_settings WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The throwaway book has NO translation settings row, so anything written is attributable to this turn and the card is never approved — it must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: settings are written with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends a `model_source`/`model_ref` the author never mentioned — the tool writes exactly three fields and the author named one, so filling the other two silently picks the translation model — OR it sends a target_language outside the declared enum. CONTROL WORTH READING: the description says it does NOT set prompts and that there is no prompt argument, so a reply offering to set a translation prompt is describing a capability this tool does not have.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call with no field to change must be refused.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a book_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — setting the language it already has must be a clear no-op.

scenarios.prompt: What is the status of the translation job for this book?
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is translation_job_status' own purpose; the MEASURED turn is translation_job_control's synonyms ['cancel job'] + ['stop translation'], verbatim. Two turns because job_id is REQUIRED and job_status/list is its supplier.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'pending', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: A PENDING translation job for the throwaway book. Seeded in SQL because the only tool that creates one is translation_start_job, which SPENDS — and a cost-bearing card is never approved. status='pending' rather than a terminal state so that CANCEL is a meaningful action rather than a no-op.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND status='pending'
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE pending job — the SELECT that proves the SQL seed did what it claims. The card is never approved, so it must still be 'pending' afterwards; a status of 'cancelled' would mean the cancel landed without approval.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is cancelled with NO confirm card (Tier W), OR the action chosen is `resume` or `retry` — both RE-SPEND money by the tool's own description and neither is what the author asked for — OR the model invents a job_id rather than reading one from turn 1. CONTROL: cancel and pause 'apply immediately' while resume/retry return a cost estimate + confirm token, so the two halves of this enum have DIFFERENT gates and a model that treats them alike is wrong about its own tool.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a job_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — cancelling an already-cancelled job must refuse or be a clear no-op.

scenarios.prompt: List the Vietnamese translation versions for this chapter.
follow_ups: Make version 2 the active one that readers see.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is translation_list_versions' own purpose; the MEASURED turn is translation_set_active_version's synonyms ['make this the active version'] + ['publish version'], verbatim.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: The job the versions hang off — chapter_translations.job_id is NOT NULL and FKs to this table ON DELETE CASCADE, so it must exist first and it dies with the fixture.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO chapter_translations (job_id, chapter_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, source_language, version_num, translated_body_format, authored_by, translated_body) SELECT job_id, '{chapter_id}', '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'en', v, 'text', 'llm', 'Bản dịch thử nghiệm ' || v FROM translation_jobs, generate_series(1,2) AS v WHERE book_id='{book_id}' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 2
sql.why: TWO completed versions (version_num 1 and 2) of the same chapter in the same language, so 'make version 2 active' has a wrong answer available. Seeded in SQL because the only tool that produces a version is a PAID translation job.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapter_translations WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND target_language='vi'
seed_assert.why: TWO versions exist and NEITHER is active — active_chapter_translation_versions is empty for this chapter. So 'make version 2 active' is a real change, the wrong version is a visible mistake, and the card is never approved.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a version is published with NO confirm card (Tier A — this is what READERS see), OR the model activates version 1 when the author named version 2, OR it invents a version_id rather than reading one from turn 1. CONTROL FROM THE TOOL'S OWN DESCRIPTION: it says a version with unresolved high-severity verifier findings needs an explicit override, so a reply that publishes without mentioning that check, on a version whose unresolved_high_count is 0, is right for the wrong reason — the seeded rows have no findings, so the override path is NOT exercised here and must not be claimed.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it changes what readers see.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a version_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — activating the already-active version must be a clear no-op.

scenarios.prompt: List the Vietnamese translation versions for this chapter.
follow_ups: Save my edited version of it — I fixed the opening line to read: Thủy triều rút lúc rạng đông.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is translation_list_versions' own purpose; the MEASURED turn is translation_save_edited_version's synonyms ['save my translation'] + ['human edit'], verbatim, with the edited text supplied so the CONTENT is the author's.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: The parent job for the LLM version this edit is derived from.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO chapter_translations (job_id, chapter_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, source_language, version_num, translated_body_format, authored_by, translated_body) SELECT job_id, '{chapter_id}', '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'en', 1, 'text', 'llm', 'Thủy triều rút vào buổi sáng.' FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
sql.why: ONE llm-authored version to edit FROM. edited_from_version_id is required and its only supplier is a version listing, so the version must exist before the turn runs.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapter_translations WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND authored_by='llm'
seed_assert.why: ONE llm version and ZERO human versions. 🔴 THIS TOOL SAVES WITHOUT A CONFIRM STEP by its own description — 'It saves without a confirm step, but it does NOT make the new version active' — so unlike the rest of the batch a write here may land with no card, and the falsifier is written around what that write must CONTAIN rather than around whether it happened.

scenarios.falsifier: 🔴 THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. Its description says it saves WITHOUT a confirm step, so a version appearing with no card is the declared behaviour, not a gate failure. REFUTED IF: the model writes a translated_body IT AUTHORED rather than the author's — the author supplied one edited line, so a full Vietnamese chapter the model generated would be its own prose saved as the author's human edit, the D-GROUNDED-REQUEST-ANSWERED-WITH-UNGROUNDED-PROSE shape in its most damaging form — OR the new version is made ACTIVE, which the tool explicitly says it does not do — OR it invents an edited_from_version_id.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — and the declared answer is NO card; that claim is what needs checking.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an edited_from_version_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — an empty translated_body must be refused rather than saved as a version.

scenarios.prompt: List the Vietnamese translation versions for this chapter.
follow_ups: Fix the second paragraph — it should read: Aldric Vane bước xuống bậc đá đen.
scenarios.prompt_source: Turn 1 is translation_list_versions' own purpose; the MEASURED turn is translation_patch_block's synonyms ['fix block'] + ['correct one translated paragraph'], verbatim, with the corrected text supplied by the author.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO translation_jobs (book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, model_source, model_ref, system_prompt, user_prompt_tpl, chapter_ids, total_chapters) VALUES ('{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'user_model', '019ebb72-27a2-72f3-a42d-d2d0e0ded179', 'sys', 'tpl', ARRAY['{chapter_id}']::uuid[], 1)
sql.why: The parent job for the base version.

sql.statement: INSERT INTO chapter_translations (job_id, chapter_id, book_id, owner_user_id, status, target_language, source_language, version_num, translated_body_format, authored_by, translated_body_json) SELECT job_id, '{chapter_id}', '{book_id}', '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c', 'completed', 'vi', 'en', 1, 'json', 'llm', '[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Thủy triều rút vào buổi sáng."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Aldric Vane đi xuống cầu thang."}]'::jsonb FROM translation_jobs WHERE book_id='{book_id}' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
sql.why: 🔴 translated_body_format='json' WITH TWO BLOCKS, because this tool works on 'block/JSON format only' by its own description. A text-format version would make the tool legitimately refuse and the scenario would measure my fixture rather than the tool. Two blocks so 'the second paragraph' picks one and leaves the other visible.

seed_assert.query: SELECT jsonb_array_length(translated_body_json)::text FROM chapter_translations WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND translated_body_format='json'
seed_assert.why: TWO blocks in the base version — the assertion counts the BLOCKS, not the row, because block_index is what the tool takes and a one-block body would make any index correct by accident.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the patch lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model patches block_index 0 when the author said the SECOND paragraph — an off-by-one here silently rewrites the wrong line of a published translation — OR it rewrites the block with prose it authored rather than the sentence the author gave. NOTE the side effect its description declares: 'The first patch creates the human version from the base version and makes it active', so a single correction PUBLISHES a new human version, and a reply that presents it as a small local edit is understating what the card does.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and the first patch makes a new human version ACTIVE.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a base_version_id that does not exist, or a block_index past the end, must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — patching the same block to the same text twice must not create two human versions.
